summary: Module 2 FIX: resolved the conflicting-assumption break via interface contracts. Step 1 -- decided WHERE the fix belongs: Task 1 was well-specified (it built the rich model: created_by owner + team_members join table with role admin/member/viewer, verified in DB); the bug was Task 2's PROMPT, which was written from my original plan (assumed teams.owner_id and a flat membership model) instead of Task 1's actual output. So Task 2 was revised, not Task 1. Step 2 -- wrote the interface contract (progress/interface-contract-m2.md) covering: exact table/column inventory (teams.id/name/created_by/created_at; team_members.id/team_id/user_id/role/created_at + uq_team_members_team_user; invitations fields), the fact that owner = teams.created_by and is NOT a team_members row, roles exactly admin|member|viewer, permission rules (membership endpoints owner-or-admin, role-change/removal owner-only), error semantics (409 dup/owner-self, 404 unknown email/member, 400 invalid role/blank name), and that TeamResponse.owner_id is presentational-only mapped from created_by. Step 3 -- re-ran the corrected Task 2 prompt with the contract embedded verbatim against the existing implementation: audit found ZERO divergences (no owner_id column anywhere, no flat-model code, role Literal enforced, require_owner_or_admin vs require_owner correct, 409 pre-check + IntegrityError rollback present), all 7 acceptance criteria confirmed live via TestClient, 75 tests green (--collect-only confirms 75 collected; my earlier '76' was a miscount of progress dots, agent was correct). Preventative rule adopted: every post-Task-1 prompt embeds the ACTUAL upstream output, never plan assumptions; schema divergence found at review -> fix the prompt, never silently patch code. This converts decomposition from splitting work into defining interfaces between pieces.
evidence: interface-contract-m2.md written: exact schema inventory + permission/error contract
